folio_note: ff. 85-177; 96 images; cipher telegrams at ff. 103, 104, 106, 107, 116, 126, 134, 138-141, 149, 151 (numeric), 153, 154. Key: GARV..1.1.4 ff. 43r-44r; Presidency key GARV..2.2.1 ff. 6v, 8, 10.
status: AGN description names cipher telegrams; the same fonds holds the key description (GARV..1.1.4, "la criptografía y descripción de claves para enviar comunicaciones", 1931) and more cipher telegrams in GARV..2.2.1 (June 1932, pliego de clave for the Presidency), GARV..2.3.1 (Oct 1932, "Comunicaciones a Presidencia en clave con traducción", radio-operator correspondence on transmission keys), GARV..2.3.2 (Oct 1932: report of Major Velasco en clave, telegrams en clave from the War Minister and Presidency) and GARV..2.4.1 (Nov 1932, "Telegramas en clave con traducción adjunta"). So the fonds has key, ciphertexts and translations, all imaged. Not on DECODE; known.py: Rodríguez Vergara no hits. Vetted 28 Oct 2026 on the scans: the telegrams of GARV..2.2.4 read with the day-of-week key of GARV..1.1.4 (f. 44r, 31 Jan 1931), e.g. f. 149 (cañonero to Caucayá, 126 men) and f. 153 (a regiment of 600 infantry and mountain artillery sent to Loreto). why: Colombian military cipher of the Leticia war (Colombia-Peru 1932-33), with the key sheet in the same private archive and images online.

seen.extent: GARV..2.2.4 holds at least 15 telegrams wholly or partly in cipher (ff. 103, 104, 106, 107, 116, 126, 134, 138, 139, 140, 141, 149, 151, 153, 154), each a few lines to half a page of letter groups; f. 151 (No. 143, 25 Sept 1932) is about 160 numbers in a different numeric system.
seen.cipher: Most telegrams are in the Colombian army's 1931 day-of-week substitution: seven alphabets (Lunes to Domingo), vowels to vowels and consonants to consonants, words forwards or reversed, with the day and D/R written in clear at the head. Cipher words are often mixed with clear words. No decipherment is written on the telegrams read here; the AGN descriptions say GARV..2.3.1 and 2.4.1 carry telegrams 'con traducción'.

vetting.key_check: The key held in the same fonds reads the telegrams. GARV..1.1.4 f. 44r ('CRIPTOGRAFIA', Bogotá 31 Jan 1931, Sección I) with the rules on f. 43r was transcribed (research/latam_vetting/1526_key_garv114.tsv). With the Lunes alphabet, f. 153 (Minguerra to Rodríguez, 26 Sept 1932) gives 'vapor Santa María ... informo ... despacharon para provincia Loreto un regimiento de infantería de seiscientos hombres y [otro] de artillería de montaña', and f. 149 (No. 141, Puerto Asís 24 Sept 1932) gives 'a la una p.m. zarpará cañonero dirección Caucayá llevando dos oficiales, ciento veintiséis tropa, noventa cajas gasolina, cincuenta galones glice[rina]'. A Sábado telegram (f. 106) gives Manao[s] and Tocantins with some typing slips. GARV..2.2.1 holds a second key, the June 1932 Presidency key (ff. 6v, 8 and 10: a 5-column letter table explained by telegraphist José Rafael Ramírez). The numeric telegram f. 151 was not tested against either key. Translations: none were seen in 2.2.4; the AGN descriptions put 'traducción' with the telegrams of GARV..2.3.1 and 2.4.1, not opened.

title: Conrad Biermann's copybook, 1675: letters outside key K55

status: Daisy (new search): "En stor del af de indførte skrivelser er i chifre." Viewed one opening (image 109): ciphertext copied into the register, clear text around it, no decipherment. title: Wallis's 'challenge' letters nos. 50, 51 and 53
correspondents: Henri Brasset → Antoine de Bordeaux-Neufville; George Villiers, 2nd Duke of Buckingham → unknown; Peter Townesend → unknown; unknown → unknown
language: French (EMLO: 'not deciphered and is in French')

folio_note: Letters 50-53 of Wallis's 'Collection of letters intercepted in cipher' (1653): no. 50 Brasset → Bordeaux 4 Apr 1653 (numeric + symbol substitution), no. 51 unknown, Scotland, 16 Jan 1651, no. 52 Buckingham, undated, no. 53 Peter Townesend, Flanders, 5 May 1658 (numeric substitution). status: EMLO notes for each: 'The letter is not deciphered; however, the cipher appears to be based on the substitution of numeric values.' The auction copy of the same collection (Dominic Winter, 7 Oct 2020, lot 375) says the last four letters are 'left unsolved as exercises for aspirant cryptographers'. The other 49 letters carry Wallis's decipherment and key, so related Royalist/French keys sit in the same volume. Not on DECODE under these shelfmarks (known.py: no hit for e Musaeo 203 / Eng. misc. e. 475 / Brasset 1653; DECODE has a different Brasset record R9429, Oct 1648). Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
why: Wallis set these as unsolved exercises; a reading would recover a 1653 French envoy's despatch on the Anglo-Dutch war and Royalist letters, and close a 370-year-old challenge.

title: German Minister at Lima: batches London could not decipher, and the Quito-Lima letter code
correspondents: German Legation Lima (Minister Perl; later Weyers) ↔ German legations in Santiago, Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Mexico
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Central Decimal File 1910-29, 862.20223 (German military activities in Peru), sub-nos. 4-99
folio_note: The 862.20223 file is scanned: M336 roll 64 (RG 64 copy, item naId 574876562), frames c. 0048-0207 and later (found 27 Oct 2026 in the NARA bulk sweep, slice J). It holds the US Legation's relays of the German code telegrams (5-figure groups), a letter code between Quito and Lima (f.0104), the Department's re-sends 'For Bell from Harrison' (f.0049-0054, 0069, 0103, 0129-0132, 0204), London's replies (f.0101 'Second undecipherable ... Fourth undecipherable'; f.0207 a verbatim English text), Lima's despatch of 6 June 1917 (f.0070-0072) and Handley's of 9 Oct 1917 (f.0205). Purport list: M973 roll 207 frames 1008-1014.
status: Partially read at the time: London (Bell / Gunther, i.e. Room 40 via the US Embassy) cabled back the 'substance' of most batches; Lima 85 (9 Oct 1917) reports some messages could not be deciphered. why: German diplomatic traffic along the west coast of South America in 1917, with a contemporary partial reading to check against.

title: Russian Foreign Ministry bigram circulars to the New York consulate, 1891-97
correspondents: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, St Petersburg (I Expédition / First Department; Obolensky, Shishkin as Adjoint) → Russian Consul General, New York (Olarovsky, Lodyzhensky)
language: Russian or French (cover text French; plaintext unknown)
shelfmark: NARA, RG 64 (microfilm M1486, Records of the Russian Consulates in the U.S., 1862-1922), roll 83, target 2 "Cables and Coded Communications, 1893-1910" (original: Russian Consulate New York, box 124); file unit naId 571170362
folio_note: Roll 83 frames 0692-1550 (target 2 starts at frame 0692). Ciphertext circulars in 2-digit bigram-key groups: f.0696-0697 (15 Dec 1906), 0698 (10 Mar 1910, No. 63637), 0712 (18 Jun 1902, No. 281), 0732 (1895, No. 4945), 0742-0743 (No. 416), 0749 (1891, No. 3313), 0751-0752 (13 Aug 1891, No. 3902, c. 330 groups, viewed: clean, no interlinear), 0755-0757 (22 Mar 1895, No. 5078), 0769-0770 (10 Mar 1895, No. 5015), 0774 (31 Dec 1904, No. 1201), 0818-0820 (May/Jul 1897, Nos. 5657, 5700), 0823, 0835-0836, 0842, 0847, 0849; the consulate's replies in cipher f.0733-0735 (No. 519, 1895, Olarovsky); 5-digit secret circular No. 864 "aux Ambassades, Légations, Consulats" f.0703-0705 (c. 350 groups, viewed: clean, groups split by hand into 3-figure parts); 5-digit cables f.0694 (cable No. 63, 22 Oct 1908), 0800-0801, 0880-0882 (Oustinoff); naval-ministry letter cipher f.0805-0807 (5-letter groups with a repeating 2849284928... key line and Russian clear text: decrypted). Key material on the same roll: instructions and worked examples for the bigram keys No. 381 (1893; f.0780-0793) and No. 389 (1900; f.0713-0727, with the 12 Dec 1865 "Pesth" example in plaintext, transposition sheet and cipher), circular on key No. 400 (1905; f.0731), additions to the dictionary key No. 402 (1910; f.0728, 0802-0803), lozungi to recipher key No. 448 "Lambda" (1915; f.0869), rules on keeping keys (f.0759-0764), Naval Ministry cipher No. 383 (f.0863-0865) and Naval key No. 394 instructions plus dictionary (f.0884-0900, 0928-1073), and decode tables (f.1088-1550, "Разборная таблица No. 404" f.1443).
status: Found in the RG 64 bulk_all hits (frames with 2-digit groups in a Russian consulate file); full roll OCR read and two frames viewed (0703, 0751). Some circulars carry the consulate's letter-by-letter decipherment worksheets on the following frames (f.0706-0711 after No. 864; 0758, 0772, 0776, 0794-0796, 0822-0825, 0837), so part of the run was read at the time; others show no worksheet in the OCR of the adjacent frames (1891 No. 3902, 1895 Nos. 4945 and 5078, 1906, 1910). The cipher system is described in full on the roll (bigram table + transposition "transparents" Lit. A/B/D; 3-figure values regrouped in 5s for the telegraph), and keys 381/389 come with plaintext-ciphertext examples. Not on DECODE; known.py: no hit for M1486, Olarovsky, Russian Consulate. Not in catalogue.json or any nara_* folder. || Brackx, issue #167 (28 Oct 2026): M1486 roll 83 (target 2, frames 0692-1550): the system is a bigram-table scheme (stencils A and D; instructions to keys 381 and 389, worked example 0790-0792); only key No. 404's tables are filmed (frames 1440-1446), so the 1888-1905 circulars' keys 356, 375, 381, 389 are not filmed; later circulars were deciphered at the time. Not checked on the film here. Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
why: A run of tsarist Foreign Ministry cipher circulars to a consulate, filed with the consulate's own key instructions and worksheets: rare primary evidence of Russian diplomatic bigram ciphers and naval codes of 1890-1910, and the unread circulars can be tested against keys and worked examples on the same roll.
